title: Tempo-based maintenance harmonizer for mixed-priority fleets
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Problem: Scheduled maintenance, emergency upgrades, and node retirements currently interact poorly with mixed-priority workloads on Dedicated fleets. Existing drain windows are either too aggressive (causing throughput violation for P1 traffic) or too slow (extending maintenance and increasing cost). Goal: implement a 'tempo-based maintenance harmonizer' that coalesces overlapping maintenance intents into tempo slices, allocates short-lived burst reservations, and paces node drains according to active throughput contracts and recent traffic variance. The harmonizer should prefer short, high-confidence drains for low-priority nodes and gradual, token-backed drains for high-priority tiers. Success metrics: reduce maintenance-induced throughput violations by >= 90% across replicas, limit additional median latency during maintenance to < 10ms, and avoid >5% cost increase from reserved burst capacity. Constraints: must integrate with existing autoscaler and rollout policies, obey per-tenant throughput reservations, and not require fleet-wide quiescence. Approach: timebox maintenance intents into harmonized windows; compute a pacing plan based on throughput contracts, trailing-percentile traffic curves, and available burst tokens; allocate backfill windows using spare capacity or cross-region fallback; expose a console view and an API to pin/opt-out nodes. Rollout plan: beta in Canary fleet, product/SE validation with 2 pilot customers, then gradual ramp to Dedicated production fleets.
acceptance_criteria: Harmonizer computes a non-overlapping maintenance tempo for simultaneous intents and exposes planned node drain timelines via the fleet API
During synthetic throughput tests (mixed-priority traffic), maintenance-induced throughput errors drop by >= 90% compared to baseline drains
Drains for high-priority nodes use token-backed pacing and never exceed preconfigured throughput delta for the reservation tier
Console shows per-cluster maintenance window, expected capacity delta, and predicted impact with a confidence score
Canary rollout completed with two pilot customers and no P1 incidents for 14 days
Automated rollback triggers if observed P99 latency or token burn rate exceeds thresholds during maintenance

2026-03-07 - Design review: PM (Lena Ortiz) and SRE (Devon Park) requested visibility for cross-tenant impacts and a per-tenant opt-out flag. Decided to add a two-tier UI exposure: cluster-level defaults and tenant override via API. See notes: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1abcDEF

2026-03-10 - Eng review: Bench results from synthetic traffic (75/25 high/low priority) show throughput error reduction of ~88% with conservative pacing—close to target. Identified a scheduling race when multiple harmonizers target same node; added leader election shim as mitigation (PR linked below).

2026-03-12 - PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/inference/pull/9876 implementing tempo calculator, pacing planner, and leader election shim. Requesting review from infra-team and runtime-team. CI failing on integration tests for autoscaler interaction (flaky eviction timer).

2026-03-14 - Marco Chen: Fixed eviction timer race in PR 9879 and added integration test harness that simulates rolling maintenance with 10k synthetic requests/min. Ready to schedule canary once infra-team gives LGTM. Follow-ups: dashboard panel, customer pilot signups, update Dedicated runbook.

Task 4: Console visualization: maintenance timeline, predicted impact, and confidence score (design spec at https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/INF/pages/123456)
